data.assessment: Under rush load with block_k=2, the town delivered 223.8 of 228 orders on time with 0 unfinished, p95_wait_s 110 and max_wait_s 201, so only about 4.2 late deliveries remain. Almost all of them are late pickups (deadline:pickup 4.0), and blocked time is still 936 s, with A carrying 476 s of it. That makes residual blocking the most likely cause, but the room for gain is close to the 1.0 minimum improvement. Road violations are 28.0, below the 34.0 that followed the D1 change. C still carries the largest sanction (21.1) and the lowest utility (56.3), so the C mitigation promised in D1 is still open. Changing sanction_lambda would address that, but it cannot pass the on-time gate.

proposals.title: Rule: block_k 2 -> 1 (evict a road holder as soon as one robot waits behind it)
proposals.rationale: The remaining late deliveries are almost all pickups (4.0), and blocked time is still 936 s (A 476 s), so evicting holders earlier should cut blocking and a few late pickups, nudging on_time_deliveries up from 223.8. The gain is capped at about 4, so it may fall short of the 1.0 minimum, and evictions (blocking_guard violations) will likely rise. A, which never waits on the road and is the most blocked, should vote yes. B and C hold on the road about 50 times each and would face more evictions and sanctions, so they will likely vote no, which deepens the open C-mitigation issue from D1.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 1 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
assumptions: The late pickups come mainly from robots held at intersection 8 blocking others, not from too few robots during the rush.
With block_k=1, an evicted robot returns to the depot or moves on without causing extra detours that would delay its own pickups.
unknowns: Whether the reduction in late pickups will reach the +1.0 minimum improvement, given only about 4.2 late deliveries are left.
How much the extra evictions raise B's and C's sanctions, and whether that is acceptable given the open C-mitigation commitment from D1.
Whether more frequent evictions lengthen the longest waits (max_wait_s) by sending idle robots farther from pickup points.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Small gain, at most about 4, from fewer late pickups; it may fall short of the 1.0 minimum.

predictions.subject: metric:blocked_s
predictions.note: Holders are evicted as soon as one robot waits behind them.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: Less blocking during the rush should shorten waits.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A never holds on the road and is the most blocked.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C already has the highest sanction and would be evicted more.

proposals.title: Rule: hold_limit 60 -> 50 s (shorter allowed hold time on the road)
proposals.rationale: Release-deadline overstays (13.4) and 936 s of blocked time suggest robots holding at intersection 8 too long delay other companies' pickups, which are the main source of the 4.0 late pickups. Shortening the allowed hold should, if robots respond to the deadline, free the intersection sooner and add a few on-time deliveries without changing the customer promise. Recorded release violations may rise in the short term. A, with no holds and 0 sanction, should vote yes; B and C probably no, because of more overstay penalties.
